blocks.content: Coastal landforms are dynamic features continuously reshaped by the relentless action of ocean waves, tides, currents, and tectonic movements.

rows: Hydraulic action, abrasion, and attrition by high-energy waves
Cliffs, Wave-cut platforms, Sea Caves, Arches, Stacks, Stumps
High-energy, rocky coastlines with strong wave action
Accumulation of sediments carried by waves and longshore drift
Beaches, Bars, Spits, Barrier Islands, Tombolos, Lagoons
Low-energy coastlines or shallow sheltered waters

items: A tombolo is a depositional landform formed when a sand ridge or spit connects an island to the mainland.
Ria coasts are formed by the submergence of river valleys, whereas Fiord/Fjord coasts are formed by the submergence of glaciated valleys.
Sequence of erosional landforms evolution: Sea Cave -> Sea Arch -> Sea Stack -> Sea Stump.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Coastal landforms are dynamically shaped by wave erosion, longshore drift, tidal fluctuations, and tectonic movements.
Marine erosional landforms include sea cliffs, wave-cut platforms, sea caves, sea arches, stacks, and stumps.
Marine depositional landforms comprise beaches, sand bars, barrier islands, spits, lagoons, and tombolos.
Submergent coastlines result from rising sea levels or tectonic subsidence, forming Ria coasts (drowned river valleys) and Fiord coasts (drowned glacial valleys).
Emergent coastlines result from falling sea levels or land uplift, featuring raised wave-cut terraces and cliffed coastlines.
